title: Sep 19 Results + Sep 20 Preview: Seven in a Row Never Looked So Easy
summary: 73.3% accuracy on Sep 19 slate. Rangers, Cubs, and Pirates delivered as expected.

content.value:
## Looking Back: Another Solid Friday Night

You know, after covering this game for three decades, I can tell you that 11-4 nights don't come around as often as the kids think they do. But when they do? You tip your cap and move on to the next slate. That's exactly what we did on September 19th—73.3% accuracy across a full Friday card. I've seen worse, and I've definitely seen better, but this one felt good.

## The Night's Highlights

The Rangers at 63% confidence? Money in the bank. The Cubs over the Reds at 61%? Just like we drew it up. But here's the thing that caught my eye—we rattled off seven consecutive correct picks from the Sox-Rays game all the way through to the Nationals-Cardinals closer. That's the kind of run that reminds you why we trust the numbers.

The three misses? Tigers couldn't get it done in Chicago, Brewers fell short in Baltimore, and the Braves couldn't quite solve Houston. Sometimes that's just baseball. The razor-thin margins on those Orioles and Mets picks at 50%? Those are essentially coin flips with a slight edge. You live with those results.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Back to the Same Well

Here's something I've learned over the years—when a matchup works once, and the circumstances stay favorable, you don't overthink it. We're going right back to Phillies-Mets on September 20th, and once again, we're backing the Mets at Citi Field.

Cristopher Sánchez takes the ball for Philadelphia, and he's been solid enough this year. But the Mets counter with Jonah Tong, and the home field advantage in a late-season divisional matchup? That's the kind of edge that's won games since they started keeping score. The model gives us a 50-50 split again, which means it's essentially a toss-up with a slight lean toward the home nine.

## The Veteran's Take

Look, I've been around long enough to know that 50% picks make some people nervous. But here's the reality of September baseball—these divisional games are tight, the rosters are deep, and sometimes the difference is just who's playing at home. The Mets have been good at Citi Field, and that's enough for me.

We'll see you back here tomorrow to see how it all shakes out. Until then, enjoy the Saturday slate.
